message_1_subject: Integration pilot & local SDK runway - post-call next steps
message_1_body:
Hi Samira —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed runway so your engineers can spin up a local pilot with minimal friction: 

TL;DR next steps (suggested cadence):
- I: Hands-on 30m pairing session (engineering-to-engineering) to run through the SDK sample apps and authenticate to a sandbox (this week)
- II: Local pilot: BrightPath engineers run 2 sample apps (chat + reranker) against a Redwood sandbox; success criteria below (2–3 days)
- III: Optional Dedicated alpha (if throughput/latency concern) or Private VPC pilot for compliance review

Success criteria for the local pilot:
- Auth: SDKs authenticate using token + optional ephemeral session (we'll provide a sandbox token)
- Routing: Requests can be routed to a dev model variant and fall back to a smaller model without changing client code
- Structured output/tool calling: Demo one structured JSON response and one tool call (webhook stub)
- Embeddings/reranker: Run embeddings on 500 test docs and confirm rerank output quality (sample eval prompt attached)

Practical SDK/runbook items I left on the call:
- Environment: Python 3.10+ virtualenv or Node 18+ (we include both examples in the sample-apps.zip)
- Auth config: API key or short-lived token; we recommend short-lived for pilots behind CI
- Local testing: Dockerfile for the sample apps + a smoke-test script (run_local.sh)
- Observability: how to read per-request cost/latency in the console (link in attachments)

Can you confirm: a) preferred slot for a 30m pairing session (I can do today 4–5pm PT or tomorrow AM), and b) any blockers (security/AV/firewall) we should pre-empt?

I’ve cc’d Karthik (integration lead) and Diego (runtime/devops) — they’ll join the pairing and provide code snippets. I attached a lightweight integration checklist and the sample-apps bundle.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

message_3_subject: Re: Integration pilot & local SDK runway - post-call next steps
message_3_body:
Perfect — locking tomorrow 10:30am PT. I've attached the sample apps bundle (Python + TypeScript examples, run_local.sh, Dockerfiles). Short answers inline and I'm looping in Karthik and Diego to follow up with concrete artifacts: 

Elliot Q1 — local GPU: yes, the SDK runs in CPU-only mode for prototyping. The sample chat app defaults to CPU fallback. We include guidance in README.md for reducing token limits and using a smaller model variant for local runs.

Elliot Q2 — rerank minibatch / quantization: for a local pilot on CPU we suggest: minibatch = 16–32 for embeddings, use 8-bit quantization (if you enable it) and run a small eval set of 200 queries. That will give you stable signal without long runtimes. For reference, our Optimize team saw diminishing returns beyond batch size 64 on CPU.

Security/compliance note: Marissa: Karthik, can you produce a short architecture note (1–2 pages) showing token handling, retention settings, and recommended KMS integration? 

Diego: can you share the Dockerfile and smoke-test command so BrightPath's infra can run the sample apps in their sandbox?

Thanks — pairing session invite incoming.

Marissa

message_4_subject: Re: Integration pilot & local SDK runway - architecture note + snippets
message_4_body:
Hi Samira / Elliot —

Attaching a short architecture note (redwood-arch-note.pdf) that covers: token lifecycle, recommended KMS flow, retention defaults for embeddings, and network egress considerations for a VPC pilot. Highlights below and a quick snippet for auth: 

Highlights: 
- Tokens: use ephemeral tokens for CI/dev. Tokens are short-lived (default 1h) and minted via a server-side exchange. Do not bake tokens into client-side code.
- Retention: embeddings default to 30 days in sandbox; configurable to 0/none for strict compliance.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS APIs (we provide example Terraform).

Auth snippet (Python):

import os
from redwood_sdk import Client

api_key = os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
client = Client(api_key=api_key)

# simple call
resp = client.chat.create(model='rwd-small-v1', messages=[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}])
print(resp)

And a TypeScript minimal example: 

import {RedwoodClient} from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY})
await client.chat.create({model: 'rwd-small-v1', messages: [{role: 'user', content: 'hi'}]})

Diego: Dockerfile and run_local.sh are in the sample-apps bundle; Diego will paste the smoke-test in the pairing session.

Looking forward to tomorrow.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
